title: The Capex Correction Continues
gist: Listed Chinese companies have been cutting capex since around 2024 and are set to keep doing so through 2026 and beyond amid weak domestic demand, which means China's excess industrial capacity should stop getting worse even as it doesn't shrink.

insights.claim: Listed Chinese companies began dialing back capital expenditures around 2024 after years of rapid investment growth, and this restraint is continuing in 2026.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Confirms a multi-year, structural pullback in Chinese corporate investment rather than a short-lived dip, relevant for gauging China industrial demand and commodity offtake.
insights.quote: After years of rapid investment growth, listed Chinese companies started to dial back their capital expenditures around 2024

insights.claim: The capex pullback among Chinese firms is driven by lackluster domestic demand, slim profit margins, tighter access to equity-market financing, and somewhat more restrained industrial-policy support.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Identifies four concrete levers (demand, margins, equity financing access, policy support) investors can track to anticipate whether the capex freeze eases or deepens.
insights.quote: a result of lackluster domestic demand, slim margins, tighter access to equity-market financing and somewhat more restrained industrial-policy support

insights.claim: Rising corporate profits in China are concentrated narrowly in electronics and commodities firms, not spread broadly across the corporate sector.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Signals a bifurcated China equity story: electronics and commodities names may be better positioned on margins/profits while the broader listed universe remains under pressure.
insights.quote: While corporate profits are up, those gains are largely confined to electronics and commodities firms.

insights.claim: Most Chinese companies outside electronics and commodities are expected to keep limiting capex through the next year and beyond because domestic demand remains persistently weak.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A multi-year capex drought in China implies subdued demand for industrial equipment, construction materials, and capital goods well past 2026.
insights.quote: For the vast majority of Chinese companies, persistently weak domestic demand means they will probably continue to limit their capex through the next year and beyond.

insights.claim: Because current Chinese corporate investment is now only enough to offset depreciation rather than expand total capacity, China's excess industrial capacity problem should stop getting worse, even though it isn't shrinking.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A stabilizing (not resolving) overcapacity picture matters for calls on Chinese producer prices, deflation exports, and global commodity/industrial-goods pricing pressure from China.
insights.quote: That caution on investment means that China’s excess capacity problems should no longer be worsening, as current rates of investment are only enough to offset depreciation and are not adding to total capacity.
